device-render.alt: Render of the final device: a voice coil motor inside a printed cage shield, bolted to a machined aluminum mount plate

exploded.alt: Labeled exploded view: voice coil motor, aluminum mount plate, piezo sensor, test beam, cage shield and centering spring

rig-photo.alt: First build of the device clamped to the machined test rig: aluminum beam on two posts over a steel base plate

sem1-exploded.alt: Exploded view of the first-semester design: open-frame shield and no centering spring

final-photo.alt: The finished device on the beam, with the printed cage shield and centering spring

fea-plate.alt: FEA displacement plot of the mount plate under the motor's 15 N peak force

control-diagram.alt: Control loop: negative acceleration feedback drives PWM to the voice coil motor, which acts on the beam, which the piezo sensor measures

test1-plot.alt: Test 1 plot: beam vibration frequency rising roughly linearly with the excitation motor's voltage

solver-failure.alt: Simulation output showing the controller's position command coming out jagged and slower than the beam

sim-result.alt: Simulated closed-loop result: beam acceleration decaying to a small steady amplitude once the controller engages

rig-cad.alt: CAD of the test rig: double-fixed beam on posts over a steel base, the device off-center and the vibration motor at the far end

wiring.alt: Wiring schematic: Arduino Uno reading the biased piezo signal and driving the voice coil motor through an L298 H-bridge from a 12 V battery
